Core intermediate deserialization routine for compiled module clusters. It drives section begin/end, iterates encoded cluster record kinds, reconstructs bindings/decls/definitions, detects malformed encodings via set_overrun, and finalizes post-processed functions. Since the report is specifically about bad compiled module cluster data, this is a prime root/intermediate candidate just beneath the diagnostic-emitting load_section path.

Highest-value deep deserializer. This very large routine reconstructs imported declarations, template decl/results, type decls, typedefs, specializations, attached entities, imported temploid friends, definitions, and merge/dedup state. The bug involves modules plus templates, and failures mention pendings for std template entities; subtle deserialization or merge-state corruption here could readily propagate into later bad-cluster or bad-pendings failures.

ranked_methods.signature: tree instantiate_decl (tree d, bool defer_ok, bool expl_inst_class_mem_p)
ranked_methods.reason: Best template-side consumer of module-loaded pending state. It explicitly calls lazy_load_pendings(d) when modules are enabled, then decides whether to defer or instantiate, and enqueues work via add_pending_template. Because the regression is about pending template entities from imported header modules, this method sits at the key module/template boundary and can expose inconsistencies in restored pending state.

It walks pending_templates, reopens instantiation levels, instantiates class/function/variable template work items, and removes completed entries. While it does not itself deserialize module data, it is where bad or inconsistent pending state restored from module files would be exercised and turned into hard failures.

ranked_methods.reason: Low-level read gate for module sections. It reads the section from ELF storage, checks size and CRC, sets E_BAD_DATA on failure, and emits section-missing/corrupted errors. Although the bug’s diagnostic is cluster-oriented rather than generic section corruption, this is a strong early validation point for malformed on-disk module data.
